description: Submission of the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026 to Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval had been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-07-01 to prepare the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026. Accordingly, the clearance of the Attorney General has been received for the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2026 prepared by the Legal Draftsman. The proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the said Bill in the Government Gazette and thereafter to submit the same to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Commissioner General of Agrarian Development
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The term of office of Mr. U.B. Rohana Rajapaksha, who is serving as the Commissioner General of Agrarian Development, is scheduled to end on 2025-10-08. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to appoint Mr. R.A.D.S. Ranatunga, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as an Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources, to the post of Commissioner General of Agrarian Development with effect from 2025-10-09, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment to the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ceylon Arts Council has been established through the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278) with the aim of promoting the fine arts, developing and encouraging indigenous arts and crafts, and providing advise to Government Departments, Regional Authorities and Institutions on any relevant matter. It has been identified that it is essential to introduce amendments to the current Arts Council Act in a manner that will enable it to maintain financial stability, including maintaining a sponsor fund for quality art research and production projects, based on the needs and expansions that have already arisen and are arising in the fields of art. It is also expected that the amendment of this Act will provide scope for intervention to ensure the professional security, dignity and well-being of artists. The Ceylon Arts Council has recommended several amendments in this regard. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to amend the Ceylon Arts Council Act, No.18 of 1952 (Chapter 278) in order to achieve broader objectives and goals than those set at the time of establishment of Ceylon Arts Council, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Formulating a new law for foster care
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been identified that there is currently no formal legal provision on foster care that covers all children in need of alternative care in Sri Lanka. Therefore, with the aim of implementing the concept of foster care (foster parenting), which is a family-based alternative care system that has become a timely need, the National Child Protection Authority has submitted a Concept Paper to establish a foster care mechanism. Through the said proposed mechanism, it is expected to implement the care programme under two main methods, namely the establishment of foster care and distance foster support. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Acting Minister of Women and Child Affairs to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a Bill to introduce a new law for foster care, based on the said Concept Paper, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No.5 of 1973
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No. 5 of 1973 has not been updated to reflect the current social and cultural trends. Today, with the advancement of communication technology, television, Internet and social media networks have spread rapidly among the people, in addition to newspapers and radio, which has had a strong impact on public life. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to amend the Sri Lanka Press Council Act, No.5 of 1973, by including provisions on the main issues of the requirement that the correction/agreement/order decided as a result of the examination conducted by the Press Council after a newspaper report was broadcast and disseminated through an electronic media should also be broadcast and disseminated by the electronic media in which the original report was broadcast and disseminated and the registration of electronic publications of printed newspapers/magazines or electronic newspapers or magazines published in the form of printed newspapers and the examination of complaints in respect thereof, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Introducing a new National Statistics Act
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The main legal framework for conducting census in Sri Lanka is the Census Ordinance No.9 of 1900. The Statistics Ordinance No.44 of 1935 has established a comprehensive statutory framework for the collection, compilation, analysis and dissemination of official statistics in Sri Lanka. However, it has been identified that the current legal framework does not provide an adequate platform for the coordination of all producers of official statistics, the integration of administrative and alternative data sources or the adoption of governance arrangements that ensure independence, impartiality and quality assurance. Therefore, a committee comprising of officers of the Department of Census and Statistics, under the technical guidance of an expert from the United Nations Statistics Division, has prepared an initial draft of the National Statistical Framework that is globally consistent and nationally compliant, combining international expertized knowledge with local institutional knowledge. The proposed initial draft seeks to modernize and unify the legal framework for the production, coordination and control of official statistics in Sri Lanka and to establish a national statistical system comprising all the producers of official statistics. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to instruct the Legal Draftsman to prepare a new Bill based on the relevant initial draft, repealing the Census Ordinance No.9 of 1900 and the Statistics Ordinance No.44 of 1935, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the 'Mission Olympics' programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has planned to implement the 'Mission Olympics 2028 - Journey to the Rings' programme to identify sportspersons who have demonstrated outstanding performance and those who may have Olympic aspirations in the future and provide them with the necessary financial and other facilities. Through this programme, sportspersons with the potential and talent to achieve international achievements in sports and win medals at the Olympic Games are to be identified and directed to long-term formal local and foreign specialized training. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports to implement the 'Mission Olympic' programme, enabling to sign contracts with such sportspersons up to the upcoming Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and to provide financial and other support for training, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Re-commencement of the currently suspended Health Care Infrastructure Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Due to the Covid-19 pandemic and the subsequent economic crisis, 33 ongoing development projects in healthcare institutions have been suspended. Considering the current state of healthcare infrastructure and the increasing demand for services, it is essential to complete those projects duly. It has been identified that the total cost estimates and project timelines of the relevant projects need to be revised, due to the suspension of the projects and the increase in the cost of construction materials and labor due to inflation, prior to the re commencement of 17 projects out of them.  Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to revise the total cost estimates of the said projects and extend the project timelines, based on the recommendations given by the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting the Presidential Media Awards Ceremony
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Although a Presidential Media Awards ceremony has been held annually to encourage journalists aiming to maintain the contents and programmes in the electronic, print and web media in Sri Lanka in a responsible, independent manner and aligned to the expectations of the audience, the said award ceremony has not been held since 2019. The said awards ceremony has been planned to resume from this year, and applications have been invited for the same, with respect to the creations of the year 2023. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to hold the Presidential Media Awards ceremony on 2025-11-11 and to increase the cash prize awarded to a winner up to Rs.100,000 and the cash prize awarded for the lifetime achievement award, which is given only once in a lifetime, up to Rs.400,000, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity of 5000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella Water Supply Scheme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Bids have been invited following the National Competitive Bidding procedure for the construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity of 5,000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella water supply scheme. Ten bidders have submitted bids for the said procurement. Based on the recommendations of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee and the Procurement Appeal Board, the proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to award the contract for the construction of a Water Treatment Plant with a capacity 5,000 cubic meters per day for the Avissawella water supply system, to M/s Sierra Construction Limited, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, was approved by the cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Dambulla Industrial Estate
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Under the "Regional Industrial Estate Development Programme" implemented by the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, 33 Industrial Estates have been constructed across the island as of now. Similarly, development work is currently underway in 07 new Industrial Estates. The Dambulla Industrial Estate has been identified as a dedicated Industrial Estate for food manufacturing and food packaging industries. For this purpose, a land in extent of 64 acres 02 roods 10.2 perches has been identified in the village of Elen Egodayaya, in the Dambulla Divisional Secretary's Division. It has been planned to develop 24 acres of land as the first phase for the proposed Industrial Estate and the remaining land in the second phase. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to allocate Rs.750 million from the provisions of the year 2025, for the development of the infrastructure facilities of the Dambulla Industrial Park and proceed with its future activities, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Allocation of additional provisions for Road Development Projects
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Out of the provisions of Rs.14,000 million allocated for the improvements of rural roads through the budget estimates for the year 2025 and rural bridges,  Rs.11,500 million has been allocated for rural road development, and subsequently, approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2025-08-11 to provide another Rs.5,000 million for the said program. The total value of projects identified for the implementation under the Rural Road Development Programme in each District by all the District Coordination Committees of the country is approximately Rs.26 billion. Taking these factors into consideration, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to allocate an additional provision of Rs.6,000 million for the Rural Road Rehabilitation and Improvement Programme by managing the local financing provisions allocated to the Ministry of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation for the year 2025.

description: Printing School Textbooks/Modules required for the year 2026
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted on 2025-06-16 to have 40% of the required school textbooks/modules for the year 2026 printed by the State Printing Corporation. In addition, 27.12 million copies of 366 types of textbooks/modules need to be printed. Accordingly, bids have been invited following the National Competitive Bidding Procedure, and 29 printing institutions have submitted bids for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to have 25.49 million copies of 362 relevant textbooks/modules printed by the said 29 institutions at a cost of Rs.3,491.47 million, based on the recommendation of the Standing High Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - In terms of the provisions of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act, No.36 of 2024, as amended by the Sri Lanka Electricity (Amendment) Act, No.14 of 2025, a Committee consisting of not more than 8 persons with at least 15 years of expertise in the fields of energy policy making, renewable energy and energy transition, energy system planning, economics and finance shall be appointed by the Minister in charge of the subject with the approval of the Cabinet of Ministers to prepare the draft National Electricity Policy as part of the National Policy on Energy. Prime Minister and with the participation of the relevant Hon. Ministers concerned, to oversee and provide guidance pertaining to the activities of the 78th Independence Day Ceremony falling on 2026-02-04

description: Allocation of land plots from Regional Industrial Estates to set up new Industries
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The selection of investors for investment in Industrial Estates is carried out by the "Regional Industrial Service Committee" established in accordance with the provisions of the Industrial Promotion Act, No.46 of 1990 and the "Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry" appointed by the Secretary to the Ministry. Accordingly, the Project Evaluation Committee of the Ministry has recommended the allocation of land plots as well, for 38 investment projects from among the 42 project proposals recommended by the Regional Industrial Service Committees. The total value of investments to be made by the said 38 investors is Rs.2,548.22 million, and it is also expected to generate about 1,559 direct employment opportunities through those industrial projects. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to provide land plots from the relevant industrial estates on lease basis for a maximum period of 35 years to the said investors, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ensuring the Sustainable Operation of Cascade System
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A group of interconnected tanks that exist within small and medium catchment areas in the dry zone of Sri Lanka is known as a Cascade System. The Cascade System, a masterpiece of Sri Lanka's irrigation civilization, has been designated a World Heritage by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). Protecting the Cascade Systems, developing them with a sustainable plan, and working to bring its benefits to society have been identified as a task that must be carried out at present. The Department of Agrarian Development has issued Circular No.06/2023 regarding the establishment of "Cascade System Management Committees" to facilitate the active participation of farmers and other stakeholders involved in economic activities related to these Cascade Systems, which protect social, economic and environmental balance, and to manage those systems while preserving them. The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to issue a new Circular jointly by the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation and the Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, enabling to establish Cascade System Management Committees, to implement the Cascade System Management Plan and to further regularize  the implementation of the relevant Committee process at district and divisional level, by amending the aforesaid Circular instructions as appropriate, and to take action to introduce amendments to the Agrarian Development Act No. 46 of 2000 to legalize the provisions of the said Circular, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Ratification of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024-12-23 to sign the Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction and establish an Inter Ministerial Committee in that regard. Accordingly, Sri Lanka has signed the said Agreement on 2025-02-20 and if Sri Lanka becomes one of the first 60 States to ratify and bring the Agreement into force and a founding member State thereof, Sri Lanka would be able to accrue numerous benefits including conservation and sustainable use of ocean’s resources and the equitable sharing of benefits derived from them. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism for Ratification of the Agreement on Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-08 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka has been identified by the Global Climate Risk Index as a country highly vulnerable to climate-related extreme weather events. It is predicted that Sri Lanka will lose more than 2% of its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) annually, due to the adverse effects of climate change. Therefore, it is estimated that the Government will need to invest approximately US$500 million annually to build climate-resilient infrastructure. The National Budget cannot afford that cost, which is about 0.5% of GDP. Therefore, a significant investment need to be made across various sectors of the economy particular in, renewable energy, agriculture, fishery industry and climate-resilient infrastructure, to mitigate and adapt to climate change. For this purpose, there is a need to create an environment that can attract green investments and mobilize private capital for climate-resilient and low-carbon sectors by introducing a more structured and formal approach to raising funds beyond traditional budgetary financing. Such an approach supports national climate priorities while also reaffirming Sri Lanka’s commitment to its international climate obligations. Focusing on these issues, the Department of External Resources and the Department of National Planning, with the participation of 35 Government institutions including the Ministry of Environment, the Department of Wildlife Conservation, the Department of Forest and in collaboration with the United Nations Development Programme, have prepared the “National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030)”. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to publish the National Climate Finance Strategy of Sri Lanka (2025-2030) and thereafter to promote and implement the said Finance Strategy, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the Supply of 120,000 Vials of Human Immunoglobulin for Intravenous use BP 5g‑6g vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - International competitive bids have been invited for the purchase of 120,000 vials of Human Immunoglobulin BP, 5-6g, for intravenous use, which is used to treat patients with immunodeficiency. Three (03) bids have been received for the same. Based on the recommendation of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee regarding the said bids, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the said procurement to Reliance Life Sciences (Pvt) Ltd., India, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder for a sum of US$ 10.506 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been invited for the procurement of Hollow Fiber Dialyzer, Polysulphone/Polyethersulphone/Polynephrone which are used for haemodialysis procedure. Two (02) bids have been received for the same. Accordingly, based on the recommendation of the Standing High‑Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the said procurement to Bain Medical Equipment (Guangzhou) Co. Ltd., China, the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a total cost of US$ 2.087 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the Supply of 30,000 vials of Tenecteplase Injection 40mg Vial
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - International competitive bids have been invited for the purchase of 30,000 vials of Tenecteplase, a vaccine used to prevent deaths in people affected with heart attacks. Three bids (03) have been received for the same. Accordingly, based on the recommendation of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the said procurement to ABC Pharma Services (Pvt) Ltd., Sri Lanka (Manufacturer: Reliance Life Sciences (Pvt) Ltd., India), the substantially responsive lowest evaluated bidder, for a total cost of Rs.2,385 million, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of Instrument Sets used for bone fixation, fracture stabilization and alignment assurance
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - International Competitive Bids have been invited for the procurement of instrument sets used for bone fixation, fracture stabilization and alignment assurance. Two (02) bids have been received for the same. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the procurement of purchasing 24 items under SR No.21209104, 30 items under SR No.21209101 and 20 items under SR No.21209004 from the said instrument sets, to Medisurg International (Pvt.) Ltd., Sri Lanka for a sum of USD 435,000, based on the recommendation of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the date of imposition of Value Added Tax (VAT) on the supply of services through electronic platforms by non-resident suppliers
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act, No.4 of 2025 has made the supply of digital services by a non-resident subject to VAT with effect from 2025-10-01. However, non-resident digital service suppliers have requested additional time to prepare for compliance with the levying of VAT on digital services, citing several practical reasons. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to amend the effective date of the relevant tax to 2026-04-01 instead of 2025-10-01 and to incorporate the relevant amending provisions in the Bill to amend the Value Added Tax Act, which is already being drafted, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the post of Director General of the Department of Census and Statistics
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Mrs. D.D.G.A. Seneviratne, who is presently serving as Director General of the Department of Census and Statistics is due to retire from the Public Service with effect from 2025-09-05 upon completion of the age of 60 years. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, to appoint Mrs. K.M.D.S.D. Karunaratne, the most senior Additional Director General of the Department of Census and Statistics to the post of Director General of that Department falling vacant, with effect from the said date, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of the fines relating to offences under the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47 of 1956, completely prohibits the employment of children below the age of 16 years and in accordance with the provisions of the said Act, regulations have been imposed to be followed by employers regarding the employment of young persons above the age of 16 but below the age of 18. According to the relevant Act and the regulations issued in accordance with the provisions of the said Act, it is a punishable offence to employ children and young persons of the relevant age group in hazardous occupation that may be detrimental to health, safety and morals. The Amendment made to the said Act in the year 2003 has introduced provisions to impose a fine not exceeding Rs.10,000/- or imprisonment for a period not exceeding 12 months or both such fine and imprisonment and also to order compensation to the prejudicated child at the discretion of the Court, on a person found guilty under the provision of the said Act. However, it has been observed that the amount of the relevant fine is inadequate. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to update and revise the minimum fines mentioned in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20(a)(3) of the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No.47, 1956, complying with the Convention No. 138 and 182 of the International Labour Organization which have been ratified by Sri Lanka, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amendment of Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing (Incorporation) Act, No.41 of 1980
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing has been incorporated by the Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing (Incorporation) Act, No.41 of 1980 and promotes marketing education by maintaining strong partnerships with the country's leading higher education institutions/universities including the Wayamba University of Sri Lanka, the Sabaragamuwa University of Sri Lanka and the Rajarata University of Sri Lanka. The Institute annually provides education to nearly 8,000 students with marketing and entrepreneurship professional qualifications and leading companies in the country obtain the services of the Institute to provide marketing training to their employees. It has been identified that the provisions of the Sri Lanka Institute of Marketing (Incorporation) Act, No.41 of 1980 should be amended to further expand the services provided by the Institute and enable it to perform more efficiently. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to amend the said Act, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation and Modernization of the Sri Lanka Planetarium
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Sri Lanka Planetarium has been designed by Dr. A.N.S. Kulasinghe and constructed as a major component of the Industrial Exhibition held in the year 1965. As the deterioration of the structure of the building and the obsolescence of its physical facilities and technical infrastructure are currently being observed, the need to modernize it while preserving its unique architectural features has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Science and Technology to assign the relevant task to the National Engineering Research and Development Centre (NERD), a premier state institution with expertise in prestressed concrete technology, based on the concurrence given by the National Procurement Commission, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Expeditiously completing the Project for renovation and conservation of the National Art Gallery
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Activities of the Project for renovation and conservation of the National Art Gallery are being carried out by the Sri Lanka Navy and approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2024‑02‑19 to complete all the activities of the project within the year 2024 itself. Nevertheless, it has not been possible to fully complete the work in the last year and a financial provision of Rs.120 million has been allocated for the same under the budget estimates for the year 2025. However, it has now been identified that the said provisions are not sufficient to fully complete the work of the project and that an additional financial provision of Rs.32 million is required. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs for securing additional budgetary provisions to complete the renovation work of the National Art Gallery expeditiously, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Conducting inquiries into complaints made with regard to missing persons
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Office on Missing Persons has been established under the provisions of the Office on Missing Persons (Establishment, Administration and Discharge of Functions) Act, No.14 of 2016. The Office is responsible for conducting investigations into missing and disappeared persons and issuing reports to their relatives. Out of the 16,966 complaints received by the said Office so far, 10,517 complaints are still pending for investigation. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Justice and National Integration to implement a special project to complete the investigations and related duties by the end of 2027 in order to provide justice to the aggrieved parties and to appoint 25 panels comprising of 75 experts including retired Judges, Senior Administrative Officers, Lawyers and other qualified persons for the relevant task, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Removal of the concessions granted in purchasing houses from the 'Viyathpura' Housing Project by the Members of Parliament
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval has been granted at the Cabinet meeting held on 2022‑07‑04 to provide 101 Housing Units from the Viyathpura Housing Complex constructed by the Urban Development Authority, for a period of one year on rent basis to the then Members of Parliament who lost their homes due to the unrest that arose in the country on 2022‑05‑09. Subsequently, those Members of Parliament have submitted requests to provide them with the opportunity to purchase those houses under a concessionary scheme. Accordingly, the Cabinet has granted its approval on 2024‑07‑15 to provide a single housing unit which is sold to general people for a minimum value of Rs.15.5 million and maximum value of Rs.22 million at a reduced minimum value of a housing unit to Rs.13.34 million and maximum value to Rs.18.21 million, to Members of Parliament under a concessional scheme, and initially charge 25% from the sale price and recover the remaining amount from them over a period of 15 years at an interest rate of 10% per annum. Twenty Nine (29) former Members of Parliament have deposited 25% of the sale price as of 2024‑12‑31 to purchase houses under the said scheme. However, due to this concessional scheme, the Urban Development Authority had to incur a loss of about Rs.92.126 million and has not been able to cover the costs incurred. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Urban Development, Construction and Housing to abolish the concessional scheme approved as referred to above with immediate effect and provide the opportunity for the 29 relevant Members of Parliament to purchase the said houses with the same method and prices applicable to the general public if they so agree, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Installation of Barricade Nets in selected perennial reservoirs to protect freshwater fish harvest
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Inland fisheries and aquaculture play a major role in providing nutritious food to the communities in rural areas. However, the washing away of fish during overflows of inland reservoirs and release of water through sluice gates has severely reduced the yield of freshwater fish. It has been identified that between 20,000 to 40,000 kilograms of fish are lost from a single freshwater reservoir per year prior to human consumption. It has been shown that washing away of mature fish leads to a decrease in fish population and the rapid depletion of future fish stocks due to the escape of sexually mature fish with breeding capacity. Therefore, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to implement a programme to install barricade nets in 250 selected perennial freshwater reservoirs within 02 years by the Sri Lanka National Aquaculture Development Authority in order to prevent the loss of freshwater fish harvest and to increase freshwater fish production, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Local assembly of a Light Train Set with three coaches
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Most of the trains currently in use are used for passenger transport in suburban areas and only a few rail buses are currently in operation to meet the transport needs of the rural community. However, practical problems have arisen in operating rail buses according to the existing train schedule. It has also been identified that it is not economically viable to deploy train sets used for operation in suburban areas to rural areas due to the lack of sufficient number of passengers. Therefore, it has been planned to introduce light train sets with three coaches for railway lines in areas such as Puttalam, Batticaloa and Mihintale which can be operated at the rural level, equipped with an electronic control system powered by a diesel engine mounted on the coaches and with other modern facilities. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation to take necessary steps to locally assemble a light train set with three coaches with a capacity of about 200 - 240 passengers and sufficient cargo space to meet the transportation needs of the rural community, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Reconstruction Project of the Sluice Tower, Sluice Barrel and remaining parts of the Senanayake Samudraya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - The Senanayake Samudraya, which was vested in the public on 1953-08-28, provides irrigated water to about 120,000 acres of paddy fields and contributes to adding 20 Megawatts of electricity to the national grid. In 1992, cracks were first observed in the sluice tower and the sluice barrel connected to the main dam and in the structure of outer spill constructed outside the main dam. Over time, these cracks have been widening and spreading. Although, it has been identified that the relevant structures should be rebuilt in order to provide a permanent solution to this, it has not been possible to construct a new sluice structure so far due to reasons such as the high cost of construction, possibility of creating a major rice shortage in the country due to the inability of providing irrigated water to a large area of ​​cultivation, consequent to the depletion of water in the reservoir for about 02 years, and the absence of adequate technical capacity. In order to mitigate the existing risk and the damage that may occur in the event of a disaster, it has been planned to maintain the total capacity of the reservoir at approximately 40% after releasing water for the Yala season 2025 and carry out the proposed construction. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to select a suitable contractor for the relevant constructions by inviting International Competitive Bids, enabling to obtain the latest technological knowledge available in the world, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Establishment of the Customs Verification Centre at Kerawalapitiya
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted at its meeting held on 2025‑03‑17 to transfer a portion of land belonging to the Sri Lanka Land Development Corporation to the Sri Lanka Customs for the establishment of the Customs Verification Centre in Kerawalapitiya, and a Committee has been appointed to determine the modality for the establishment of the said Customs Verification Centre. The said Committee has submitted its recommendations with appropriate criteria for selecting a more viable business modality. Accordingly, based on the recommendation of the said Committee, the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to follow the procedure for calling Expressions of Interest and Requests for Proposal to select a suitable Private Partner to implement the proposed Kerawalapitiya Customs Verification Centre project under a Hybrid Public-Private Partnership Model.

description: Establishment of Diplomatic relations with Antigua and Barbuda
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Approval of the Cabinet has been granted previously to establish formal diplomatic relations with 13 countries in the Latin American and Caribbean region. Accordingly, required measures have already been taken by the Government of Sri Lanka as of now to establish diplomatic relations with the countries of the region, other than Antigua and Barbuda. The proposal made by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism to sign the Agreement on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations between the Government of Sri Lanka and the Government of Antigua and Barbuda, aiming to accrue mutual benefits by both countries and enhance existing friendly relations and cooperation in the political, socio-economic and cultural fields, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Closure of Non-Functioning State-Owned Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Some State‑Owned Enterprises established long ago to achieve the objectives such as providing public services and promoting strategic economic activities have become inactive due to reasons such as continuation of those enterprises is not practical owing to the incompatibility of the objectives of their establishment with the present mandate and market requirements and financial underperformance. It has been identified as appropriate to liquidate and close down State-Owned Enterprises belonging to various categories such as Statutory Bodies, State Corporations and State-Owned Companies that do not make a meaningful contribution to the national economy or the public service delivery, instead of continuing to operate them as a burden to the Government. Accordingly, taking into consideration the proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development, the approval of the Cabinet was granted to formally liquidate and close down 33 State-Owned Enterprises that are not-functioning at present, in 02 stages under the supervision of a special liquidation unit to be established under the said Ministry.

description: Admission of Students from Grade 2 to 11 except Grade 5 and 6 in Schools
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-09-03 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Maintenance of the number of students in a classroom, only within the approved limits is essential to implement the new proposed education reforms. Therefore, it has been identified that it would be appropriate to introduce a proper mechanism to provide the opportunity to admit students to intermediate grades other than Grades 5 and 6 in schools, while ensuring the right of all children in the country for education. Taking into account the said matters, it has been planned to issue new circular instructions to provide the opportunity to apply for the intermediate grades in other schools, so that priority is given to students genuinely need to be admitted to another school from the school they are currently studying, for various reasons. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Hon. Prime Minister in her capacity as the Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education to cancel the circular instructions  issued so far pertaining to the admission of students from Grade 2 to Grade 11 other than Grade 5 and 6 in schools and issue new circular instructions for the same, taking into considerations the recommendations made by the Parliamentary Sub‑Committee appointed by the Advisory Committee of the  Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Posts of District Secretaries/Government Agents of the Administrative Districts of Kalutara and Puttalam
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The proposal made by the Minister of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government to appoint Mr.H.M.S.P Herath, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as the District Secretary/Government Agent of the Administrative District of Puttalam, to the Post of District Secretary/Government Agent of the Administrative District of Kalutara and to appoint Mr. Y.I.M Silva, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service, presently serving as an Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, to the post of District Secretary/Government Agent of the Administrative District of Puttalam which falls so vacant, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Pricing Mechanism of Medicines in accordance with the National Medicines Regulatory Authority Act No. 5 of 2015
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The Medicines (Pricing Mechanism for Medicines) Regulations No. 02 of 2025, have been issued introducing pricing mechanism for the Maximum Retail Price for an individual product and the pricing mechanism for the Maximum Ceiling Price for a dosage form and strength of a particular medicine or a particular group of medicines and the said Regulations have been published through the Gazette Extraordinary Notification No. 2446/34 dated 2025 07 21. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to submit the relevant Regulations to Parliament for approval, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of Standby Power Supply Systems for the Condenser Cooling System and the Boiler Feed Water System of the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Coal Power Plant
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The auxiliary power supply of the Condenser Cooling System and the Boiler Feed Water System of the Norochcholai Lakvijaya Coal Power Plant become inoperative during an island-wide power outage as there is no auxiliary power supply available at the Plant for safe plant shut down. The operations of the Plant have to be shut down for 4 or 5 days to allow for cooling, thereby resulting a significant financial loss. The Committee appointed to find a technically sound solution to avoid this situation, has suggested that it is appropriate to introduce a seamless standby auxiliary power supply for critical systems that can be implemented within a short period of time. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Energy to implement a project to operate an auxiliary power supply for the Condenser Cooling System and the Boiler Feed Water System using the funds of the Ceylon Electricity Board, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement of 1,500,000 Bbls of Gasoline 92 Unl during the period from 2025 09 15 to 2026 03 14
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: Bids have been invited to meet the requirement of 1,500,000 Bbls +/-5% of Gasoline 92 Unl for a period of six (06) months from 2025 09 15 to 2026 03 14, from the suppliers registered of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation. Eight (08) suppliers have submitted bids for the purpose. The proposal made by the Minister of Energy to award the term contract for the supply of 1,500,000 Bbls +/-5% of Gasoline 92 Unl (05 shipments of 300,000Bbls +/-5% each) to M/s. Aditya Birla Global Trading (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., Singapore, based on the recommendation of the Special Standing Cabinet Appointed Procurement Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Protection of the Temple on Pillars (Tampita Vihare) of Bingiriya Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: Bingiriya Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare is a temple established during the period of the Anuradhapura Kingdom. A monks' residence (Avasaya) with wooden pillars believed to have been built after the said era and the largest temple on pillars (Tampita Vihare) in South Asia built during the Kandyan Kingdom, a stupa, a parapet wall for the Bodhi and a belfry belonging to the British era are located on this temple premises. This Tampita Vihare, believed to have been built under the patronage of King Keerthi Sri Rajasinghe, is constructed 40 feet in length and 24 feet in width on 24 stone pillars each 06 feet high. Wooden joints unique to the architectural craftsmanship of the Kandyan era, old wall paintings and statues are also found in the temple. However, it has been observed that most of the beams of the temple have decayed due to environmental factors and biological activities, and the Department of Archaeology has now commenced conservation activities of the temple. The Expert Committee appointed to propose a methodology for the conservation of the Tampita Vihare of the Devagiri Rajamaha Vihare has suggested that it is appropriate to construct a protective roof for the conservation of the Tampita Vihare. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to have the proposed protective roof of the Tampita Vihare constructed by the Department of Government Factory using the provisions provided by the Central Cultural Fund, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Procurement for the supply of 20,000 of Nanocrystal Silver Dressing (20cm x 40cm in size)
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: International competitive bids have been invited for the procurement of 20,000 Nanocrystal Silver Dressings (20cm x 40cm in size) used for the treatment and management of wounds. Only one bid has been received for the same. Accordingly, based on the recommendation of the Standing High-Level Procurement Committee, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to award the relevant procurement to CIC Holdings PLC, Sri Lanka (Manufacturer: Smith & Nephew Medical Limited, United Kingdom) the only responsive bidder, for a sum of Rs. 639.5 million (+VAT), was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Rehabilitation of the stretch between Kottawa and Dodangoda of the Southern Expressway from 19thkm to 34thkm
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: Extensive surface cracking and degradation of underlying structural layers have been observed in the stretch between Kottawa and Dodangoda of the Southern Expressway from 19thkm to 34thkm. Therefore, it has been identified that the said section of road needs to be rehabilitated, the base failures be rectified and a resurfacing be made. For this purpose, bids have been invited from qualified local firms, following the National Competitive Bidding procedure. After evaluating the bids received, the Standing High Level Procurement Committee has recommended awarding the contract to MAGA Engineering (Pvt) Ltd., the substantially responsive lowest bidder. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Transport, Highways, Ports and Civil Aviation, to award the relevant contract to MAGA Engineering (Private) Limited, based on the said recommendation, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of Mental Health Awareness and Counseling Programme
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: A high rate of suicide, increase in drug use and increased emergence of psychosocial issues, especially among adolescents and young adults, among Sri Lankans, have been observed. Accordingly, as per a budget proposal of 2025, provisions amounting to Rs. 250 million have been allocated to implement a special programme to address mental health issues. Under that, the Ministry of Health and Mass Media has proposed to implement a medium-term programme aiming to expand awareness and counseling services for school children and adolescents. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Health and Mass Media to implement the proposed programme in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education, the National Dangerous Drugs Control Board, the National Institute of Mental Health, provincial and district health services, hospitals and other relevant institutions, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Bay of Bengal Regional Plan of Action to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The International Plan of Action to Prevent, Deter and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing was unanimously adopted by the member States of the Food and Agriculture Organization in 2001 with the aim of restoring depleted fish stocks and ensuring food security. Consequently, Sri Lanka has also prepared a National Action Plan for the same. Similarly, the member States of the Bay of Bengal Programme Inter-Governmental Organization, have collectively agreed to sign a Regional Plan of Action to address illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing in the region. The Plan aims to strengthen the prevention, deterrence and elimination of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing in the exclusive economic zones of Bangladesh, India, Maldives and Sri Lanka, as well as in the surrounding seas and oceans beyond national jurisdiction. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Fisheries, Aquatic and Ocean Resources to sign the said Regional Plan of Action, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Memorandum of Understanding between the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation and the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences on Agricultural Cooperation
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The Ministry in charge of the subject of Agriculture has implemented the Project ‘Technical Assistance under South-South Cooperation with the People’s Republic of China’ with the aim of improving the banana, mango and pineapple value chains in Sri Lanka. This project, which was technically supported by the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences, has introduced innovative technologies and practices that can significantly increase yields, improve the availability of planting materials, strengthen post-harvest practices and promote value addition across the fruit cultivation sector. It has been observed that it would be appropriate to establish a formal mechanism to continue the existing collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences beyond the current project period so that the benefits of the said project can be fully and sustainably realized. It is proposed to make the opportunity for germplasm exchange of fruit crops in accordance with the existing Acts and Regulations, promote exchange of scholars and experts to support technological advancement of both parties, and support capacity building of processors, traders and other value chain actors. The proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Lands and Irrigation to sign the Memorandum of Understanding on Agricultural Cooperation between the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation and the Chinese Academy of Tropical Agricultural Sciences for that purpose, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Implementation of the Project ''Fostering Sustainable Economic Recovery through Improved Biodiversity and Sustainable Waste Management''
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: The Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government, together with the European Union, has prepared a project proposal to implement initiatives on biodiversity conservation and solid waste management in the Central, Uva, North Western, North Central and Northern Provinces. Protecting high-value biodiversity sites by restoring degraded ecosystems, implementing targeted conservation strategies and promoting sustainable land-use practices is one of the objectives of this project. Further, implementation of sustainable waste management practices in selected local authority areas, promotion of climate resilient practices, and conducting capacity building programmes for local communities, government agencies and the private sector are also expected through this project. The relevant project is planned to be implemented through a Grant of EURO 8 million of the European Union. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to sign the Financing Agreement with the European Union for obtaining the relevant Grant to implement the said Project, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Appointment to the Post of Director General of Export Agriculture
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Ms. A.P.P. Disna, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service, who held the Post of Director General of the Department of Export Agriculture, has retired from the Public Service by now. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock, Land and Irrigation to appoint Mrs. M.K.S.R.D. Samarasinghe, Special Grade Officer of the Sri Lanka Scientific Service, presently serving as the Additional Director General (Research) of the said Department, to the Post of Director General of the Department of Export Agriculture with immediate effect, was approved by the Cabinet.

description: Amending the National Museums Ordinance No. 31 of 1942
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-08-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - It has been found necessary to amend the National Museums Ordinance No. 31 of 1942 which is in force at present with the objectives of preservation of artefacts,  determining penalties for offences involving artefacts, introduction of criteria for categorization of objects in the process of collecting artefacts, establishment of new museums, regulation of existing museums, expansion of the scope of museums and strengthening the administration structure. Accordingly, approval of the Cabinet has previously been granted to appoint a Committee comprising of experts in the relevant field to identify necessary amendments to amend the said Ordinance and obtain technical information required thereto. As such, the proposal made by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to amend the said National Museums Ordinance, based on the recommendations in the Report submitted by the said Committee, was approved by the Cabinet.
